claim: β-selection is the most pivotal event determining αβ T cell fate.
source: β-selection is the most pivotal event determining αβ T cell fate.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about T cell development.

claim: Surface-expression of a pre-T cell receptor (pre-TCR) induces thymocyte metabolic activation, proliferation, survival and differentiation during β-selection.
source: Here, surface-expression of a pre-T cell receptor (pre-TCR) induces thymocyte metabolic activation, proliferation, survival and differentiation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about pre-TCR function cited in the abstract.

claim: β-selection requires co-stimulatory signals from Notch receptors.
source: Besides the pre-TCR, β-selection also requires co-stimulatory signals from Notch receptors - key cell fate determinants in eukaryotes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about β-selection requirements.

claim: Notch-dependence of β-selection is established through antagonistic signaling by PI3K and Itpkb.
source: Here, we show that this Notch-dependence is established through antagonistic signaling by the pre-TCR/Notch effector, phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K), and by inositol-trisphosphate 3-kinase B (Itpkb).
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: PI3K is canonically counteracted by the lipid-phosphatases Pten and Inpp5d/SHIP-1.
source: Canonically, PI3K is counteracted by the lipid-phosphatases Pten and Inpp5d/SHIP-1.
evidence: This is established knowledge about canonical PI3K regulation.

claim: Itpkb dampens pre-TCR induced PI3K/Akt signaling by producing IP4, a soluble antagonist of PIP3.
source: In contrast, Itpkb dampens pre-TCR induced PI3K/Akt signaling by producing IP4, a soluble antagonist of the Akt-activating PI3K-product PIP3.
evidence: This is a key finding of the study supported by experimental data showing Akt hyperactivation in Itpkb-/- cells.

claim: Itpkb-/- thymocytes are pre-TCR hyperresponsive.
source: Itpkb-/- thymocytes are pre-TCR hyperresponsive, hyperactivate Akt, downstream mTOR and metabolism, undergo an accelerated β-selection and can develop to CD4+CD8+ cells without Notch.
evidence: This is supported by data showing increased Nr4a1/Nur77-GFP expression and activation markers in Itpkb-/- cells (Figures 3B, 6I).

claim: Itpkb-/- thymocytes hyperactivate Akt.
source: Itpkb-/- thymocytes are pre-TCR hyperresponsive, hyperactivate Akt, downstream mTOR and metabolism, undergo an accelerated β-selection and can develop to CD4+CD8+ cells without Notch.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing increased phospho-Akt levels in Itpkb-/- TCRβ+ DN3 cells (Figure 8A).

claim: Itpkb-/- thymocytes hyperactivate mTOR.
source: Itpkb-/- thymocytes are pre-TCR hyperresponsive, hyperactivate Akt, downstream mTOR and metabolism, undergo an accelerated β-selection and can develop to CD4+CD8+ cells without Notch.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing increased phospho-mTOR levels in Itpkb-/- TCRβ+ DN3 cells (Figure 8A).

claim: Itpkb-/- thymocytes undergo accelerated β-selection.
source: Itpkb-/- thymocytes are pre-TCR hyperresponsive, hyperactivate Akt, downstream mTOR and metabolism, undergo an accelerated β-selection and can develop to CD4+CD8+ cells without Notch.
evidence: This is supported by data showing faster DP cell generation in multiple experimental systems (Figures 5C, 6F, 7A-D).

claim: Itpkb-/- thymocytes can develop to CD4+CD8+ cells without Notch.
source: Itpkb-/- thymocytes are pre-TCR hyperresponsive, hyperactivate Akt, downstream mTOR and metabolism, undergo an accelerated β-selection and can develop to CD4+CD8+ cells without Notch.
evidence: This is supported by data showing DP cell generation from Itpkb-/- DN3 cells on OP9 stroma lacking Notch ligands (Figures 7A,B, 9B) and resistance to γ-secretase inhibitor (Figure 10).

claim: Inhibition of Akt reverses the accelerated β-selection phenotype of Itpkb-/- thymocytes.
source: This is reversed by inhibition of Akt, mTOR or glucose metabolism.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that Akt-inhibitor VIII treatment restores WT-like DP cell generation from Itpkb-/- DN3 cells (Figure 9A).

claim: Inhibition of mTOR reverses the accelerated β-selection phenotype of Itpkb-/- thymocytes.
source: This is reversed by inhibition of Akt, mTOR or glucose metabolism.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that rapamycin treatment restores WT-like DP cell generation from Itpkb-/- DN3 cells (Figures 7C,D, 9A).

claim: Inhibition of glucose metabolism reverses the accelerated β-selection phenotype of Itpkb-/- thymocytes.
source: This is reversed by inhibition of Akt, mTOR or glucose metabolism.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that 2-deoxy-D-glucose treatment restores WT-like DP cell generation from Itpkb-/- DN3 cells (Figure 9A).

claim: Thymocytes develop from bone marrow progenitors through successive CD4-CD8- double-negative stages DN1, DN2, DN3 and DN4.
source: Thymocytes develop from bone marrow (BM) progenitors through successive CD4-CD8- 'double-negative' CD44+CD25-c-Kit+ DN1, CD44+CD25+c-Kit+ DN2, HSAhighc-Kit-CD44-CD25+ DN3 and HSAhighCD44-CD25- DN4 stages (Petrie and Zuniga-Pflucker, 2007; Xiong et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about thymocyte development, supported by citations.

claim: Productive rearrangement of one TCRβ-allele causes surface-expression of a pre-TCR on DN3 cells.
source: Productive rearrangement of one TCRβ-allele causes surface-expression of a pre-TCR comprised of TCRβ, pre-TCRα and signal-transducing CD3 subunits on DN3 cells (Aifantis et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about pre-TCR expression, supported by citation.

claim: At β-selection, ligand-independent pre-TCR signaling triggers DN3 cell metabolic activation, proliferation and survival.
source: At the first checkpoint, β-selection, ligand-independent pre-TCR signaling triggers DN3 cell metabolic activation, proliferation and survival.
evidence: This is established knowledge about β-selection, supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Pre-TCR signaling triggers allelic exclusion of the second TCRβ allele.
source: It also triggers allelic exclusion of the second TCRβ allele, initiation of TCRα gene-rearrangements and differentiation via CD8+HSAhighTCRβlow immature single positive (ISP) precursors into CD4+CD8+ 'double-positive' (DP) cells (Petrie and Zuniga-Pflucker, 2007; Xiong et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about pre-TCR signaling effects, supported by citations.

claim: β-selection ensures that only DN3 cells expressing a functional TCRβ chain develop further.
source: β-selection ensures that only DN3 cells expressing a functional TCRβ chain develop further.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of β-selection.

claim: Defective β-selection causes a DN3 block and severe immunodeficiency.
source: Defective β-selection causes a DN3 block and severe immunodeficiency (Juntilla and Koretzky, 2008; Aifantis et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Pre-TCR signaling alone is insufficient for DN-to-DP cell differentiation without co-stimulation by thymic microenvironmental signals.
source: pre-TCR signaling alone is insufficient for DN-to-DP cell differentiation without co-stimulation by thymic microenvironmental signals.
evidence: This is established knowledge about β-selection requirements.

claim: Ligand engagement of Notch on DN3/DN4 cells promotes nutrient receptor expression, glucose uptake, metabolism, growth, survival, proliferation and differentiation.
source: In particular, ligand engagement of Notch on DN3/DN4 cells promotes nutrient receptor expression, glucose uptake, metabolism, growth, survival, proliferation and differentiation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Notch signaling effects, supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Excessive Notch signaling causes thymocyte transformation and T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL).
source: But excessive Notch signaling causes thymocyte transformation and T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Notch signaling in disease, supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Pre-TCR signals augment T-ALL caused by excessive Notch signaling.
source: This is augmented by pre-TCR signals (Ciofani et al., 2004; Ciofani and Zuniga-Pflucker, 2005; Campese et al., 2006; Fayard et al., 2010; Taghon et al., 2006; Aifantis et al., 2006; Tussiwand et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Both pre-TCR and Notch activate phosphatidylinositol 3-kinases (PI3K).
source: Both pre-TCR and Notch activate phosphatidylinositol 3-kinases (PI3K) (Ciofani and Zuniga-Pflucker, 2005; Juntilla and Koretzky, 2008; Fayard et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: PI3K phosphorylate PIP2 into PIP3.
source: PI3K phosphorylate the membrane lipid phosphatidylinositol(4,5)bisphosphate (PIP2) into phosphatidylinositol(3,4,5)trisphosphate (PIP3).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PI3K enzymatic activity.

claim: PIP3 recruits and activates Itk/Tec-, Pdk1-, and Akt-family kinases by binding to their PH domains.
source: PIP3 recruits and activates Itk/Tec-, Pdk1-, and Akt-family kinases by binding to their PH domains.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PIP3 signaling mechanisms.

claim: PI3K are essential and rate-limiting for β-selection by promoting metabolism, proliferation, survival and differentiation.
source: PI3K are essential and rate-limiting for β-selection by promoting metabolism, proliferation, survival and differentiation (Juntilla and Koretzky, 2008; Fayard et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Itk promotes activation of phospholipase-Cγ1 (PLCγ1).
source: Itk promotes activation of phospholipase-Cγ1 (PLCγ1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Itk function.

claim: PLCγ1 hydrolyzes PIP2 into IP3 and diacylglycerol (DAG).
source: PLCγ1 hydrolyzes PIP2 into the second messengers inositol(1,4,5)trisphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol (DAG), which then convey downstream signals (Aifantis et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PLCγ1 enzymatic activity, supported by citation.

claim: Itk loss only subtly impairs β-selection.
source: Itk loss only subtly impairs β-selection (Lucas et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Pdk1 is required for DN3/DN4 cell differentiation mostly by activating Akt.
source: Pdk1 is required for DN3/DN4 cell differentiation mostly by activating Akt, and for thymocyte proliferation through other effectors (Kelly et al., 2007; Fayard et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Akt kinases are required for β-selection by promoting DN3/DN4 cell glucose uptake, glycolysis, viability and differentiation.
source: Akt kinases are required for β-selection by promoting DN3/DN4 cell glucose uptake, glycolysis, viability and differentiation (Juntilla et al., 2007; Fayard et al., 2007; Mao et al., 2007; Fayard et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: mTORC2 and possibly mTORC1 have important roles in β-selection.
source: Recent studies suggest important roles for the Akt activator mTORC2 and possibly the Akt downstream-effector mTORC1 in β-selection (Lee et al., 2012; Tang et al., 2012; Chou et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Inpp5d/SHIP1-/- early thymocytes develop normally.
source: Inpp5d/SHIP1-/- early thymocytes develop normally (Kashiwada et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Conditionally Pten-/- DN cells show constitutively active Akt and accelerated development to DP cells.
source: Conditionally Pten-/- DN cells show constitutively active Akt and accelerated development to DP cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Pten-/- DN cells can generate DP cells without pre-TCR or Notch-signaling.
source: They can generate DP cells without pre-TCR or Notch-signaling (Hagenbeek et al., 2004; Kelly et al., 2007; Shiroki et al., 2007; Wong et al., 2012; Hagenbeek et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Notch may promote DN3/DN4 cell survival and differentiation in part by repressing Pten.
source: Notch may promote DN3/DN4 cell survival and differentiation in part by repressing Pten (Wong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: IP3 can be phosphorylated into IP4 by four mammalian IP3 3-kinases.
source: IP3 is well known to mobilize Ca2+ but can also be phosphorylated into inositol(1,3,4,5)tetrakisphosphate (IP4) by four mammalian IP3 3-kinases (Sauer and Cooke, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Itpkb is an essential TCR effector.
source: Among these, we and others have identified Itpkb as an essential TCR effector.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior work by the authors and others.

claim: Thymocyte development in Itpkb-/- mice is blocked at the DP stage due to defective positive selection.
source: Thymocyte development in Itpkb-/- mice is blocked at the DP stage due to defective positive selection (Huang et al., 2007; Pouillon et al., 2003; Wen et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior publications, supported by citations.

claim: TCR signaling activates Itpkb to produce IP4.
source: In thymocytes, TCR signaling activates Itpkb to produce IP4, a soluble analog of the PH domain binding moiety of PIP3.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior work.

claim: Itpkb-/- thymocytes have strongly reduced IP3 3-kinase activity and IP4 levels.
source: Itpkb-/- thymocytes have strongly reduced IP3 3-kinase activity and IP4 levels, but normal IP3 levels and Ca2+ mobilization (Pouillon et al., 2003; Wen et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior publications, supported by citations.

claim: Itpkb-/- thymocytes have normal IP3 levels and Ca2+ mobilization.
source: Itpkb-/- thymocytes have strongly reduced IP3 3-kinase activity and IP4 levels, but normal IP3 levels and Ca2+ mobilization (Pouillon et al., 2003; Wen et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior publications, supported by citations.

claim: IP4 can bind to PH domains and control PIP3 binding.
source: IP4 can bind to PH domains and control PIP3 binding (Huang et al., 2007; Jia et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In NK cells, myeloid cells and hematopoietic stem cells, IP4 competitively limits PIP3-binding to and activation of Akt.
source: In NK cells, myeloid cells and hematopoietic stem cells (HSC), IP4 competitively limits PIP3-binding to, and activation of Akt (Jia et al., 2008; 2007; Sauer et al., 2013; Siegemund et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior publications, supported by citations.

claim: DN3 cells from Itpkb+/+Rag2-/- but not Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- mice express Itpkb.
source: DN3 cells from Itpkb+/+Rag2-/- but not Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- mice express Itpkb (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Itpkb-/- mice had increased DN3 and reduced DN4 cell proportions compared to controls.
source: Compared to controls, Itpkb-/- mice had increased DN3 and reduced DN4 cell proportions with a ~three-fold increased DN3:DN4 ratio (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Itpkb-/- mice had a ~three-fold increased DN3:DN4 ratio compared to controls.
source: Compared to controls, Itpkb-/- mice had increased DN3 and reduced DN4 cell proportions with a ~three-fold increased DN3:DN4 ratio (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Itpkb-/- mice had WT-like total thymic cellularity.
source: Surprisingly, Itpkb-/- mice had WT-like total thymic cellularity and numbers of DN3 cells and CD25int 'DN3-4' intermediates between DN3 and DN4 cells (Xiong et al., 2011) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Itpkb-/- mice had WT-like numbers of DN3 cells.
source: Surprisingly, Itpkb-/- mice had WT-like total thymic cellularity and numbers of DN3 cells and CD25int 'DN3-4' intermediates between DN3 and DN4 cells (Xiong et al., 2011) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Itpkb-/- mice had WT-like numbers of DN3-4 intermediate cells.
source: Surprisingly, Itpkb-/- mice had WT-like total thymic cellularity and numbers of DN3 cells and CD25int 'DN3-4' intermediates between DN3 and DN4 cells (Xiong et al., 2011) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Itpkb-/- DN3, DN3-4 and DN4 cells contained WT amounts of total TCRβ and CD3 protein.
source: Itpkb-/- DN3, DN3-4 and DN4 cells contained WT amounts of total TCRβ and CD3 protein (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Surface TCRβ/CD3 amounts on DN3 and DN3-4 cells were similar between Itpkb-/- and WT mice.
source: These were similar between genotypes (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The proportion of Lin-HSAhigh DN4 cells expressing surface TCRβ/CD3 was reduced in Itpkb-/- vs. WT mice.
source: In contrast, the proportion of Lin-HSAhigh DN4 cells expressing surface TCRβ/CD3 was reduced in Itpkb-/- vs. WT mice.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Itpkb-/- mice had significantly less TCRβ- DN4 and ISP cells compared to WT mice.
source: Compared to WT mice, Itpkb-/- mice had significantly less TCRβ- DN4 and ISP cells, but similar DP cell numbers and an increased (DN3 + DN3-4):TCRβ- DN4 cell ratio (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Itpkb-/- mice had similar DP cell numbers compared to WT mice.
source: Compared to WT mice, Itpkb-/- mice had significantly less TCRβ- DN4 and ISP cells, but similar DP cell numbers and an increased (DN3 + DN3-4):TCRβ- DN4 cell ratio (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Itpkb-/- mice had an increased (DN3 + DN3-4):TCRβ- DN4 cell ratio compared to WT mice.
source: Compared to WT mice, Itpkb-/- mice had significantly less TCRβ- DN4 and ISP cells, but similar DP cell numbers and an increased (DN3 + DN3-4):TCRβ- DN4 cell ratio (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Itpkb-/- DN3-4 cells had increased CD2 levels compared to WT controls.
source: Compared to WT controls, Itpkb-/- DN3-4 cells and later stages had increased CD2 levels and normal to increased surface levels of CD5, CD27 and CD71 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Itpkb-/- DN3-4 cells had normal to increased surface levels of CD5, CD27 and CD71 compared to WT controls.
source: Compared to WT controls, Itpkb-/- DN3-4 cells and later stages had increased CD2 levels and normal to increased surface levels of CD5, CD27 and CD71 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Itpkb-/- DN3-4 and DN4 cells had elevated surface-levels of CXCR4 compared to WT controls.
source: Also, Itpkb-/- DN3-4 and DN4 cells had elevated surface-levels of the costimulatory chemokine-receptor and Notch-target CXCR4 (Trampont et al., 2010; Xie et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Itpkb-/- and WT DN3, DN3-4 and TCRβ- DN4 cells each expressed comparable surface CD28, CD127 and CD98.
source: In contrast, Itpkb-/- and WT DN3, DN3-4 and TCRβ- DN4 cells each expressed comparable surface CD28, CD127 and CD98.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: DN3 and later stages of thymocyte development expressed more Nr4a1/Nur77-GFP in Itpkb-/- than WT mice.
source: Supporting pre-TCR hyper-responsiveness, DN3 and later stages of thymocyte development expressed more Nr4a1/Nur77-GFP in Itpkb-/- than WT mice (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Ki67-staining suggests comparable steady-state proliferation of all thymocyte subsets between Itpkb-/- and WT genotypes.
source: But similar Ki67-staining and in vivo BrdU incorporation suggest comparable steady-state proliferation of all thymocyte subsets between genotypes (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In vivo BrdU incorporation suggests comparable steady-state proliferation of all thymocyte subsets between Itpkb-/- and WT genotypes.
source: But similar Ki67-staining and in vivo BrdU incorporation suggest comparable steady-state proliferation of all thymocyte subsets between genotypes (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: AnnexinV staining suggests comparable viability of thymocyte subsets between Itpkb-/- and WT genotypes.
source: Similar AnnexinV staining suggests comparable viability (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Itpkb-/- donor-derived thymocytes reproduced the increased DN3 and reduced DN4 cell proportions in mixed bone marrow chimeras.
source: Compared to WT controls, Itpkb-/- donor-derived thymocytes reproduced the published cell-intrinsic block at the DP stage (Wen et al., 2004) and the increased DN3 and reduced DN4 cell proportions, partial loss of TCRβ- DN4 and ISP cells, and increased (DN3 + DN3-4):TCRβ- DN4 cell ratio of Itpkb-/- mice (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from mixed BM chimeras shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Itpkb-/- donor-derived thymocytes showed partial loss of TCRβ- DN4 and ISP cells in mixed bone marrow chimeras.
source: Compared to WT controls, Itpkb-/- donor-derived thymocytes reproduced the published cell-intrinsic block at the DP stage (Wen et al., 2004) and the increased DN3 and reduced DN4 cell proportions, partial loss of TCRβ- DN4 and ISP cells, and increased (DN3 + DN3-4):TCRβ- DN4 cell ratio of Itpkb-/- mice (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from mixed BM chimeras shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Itpkb-/- vs. WT donor-derived DN3-4 and DN4 cells overexpressed CD2 in mixed bone marrow chimeras.
source: Moreover, Itpkb-/- vs. WT donor-derived DN3-4 and DN4 cells overexpressed CD2 and tended to upregulate CXCR4 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from mixed BM chimeras shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Itpkb-/- vs. WT donor-derived DN3-4 and DN4 cells tended to upregulate CXCR4 in mixed bone marrow chimeras.
source: Moreover, Itpkb-/- vs. WT donor-derived DN3-4 and DN4 cells overexpressed CD2 and tended to upregulate CXCR4 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from mixed BM chimeras shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Ki67 staining was similar between Itpkb-/- and WT genotypes in mixed bone marrow chimeras.
source: Ki67 staining was again similar between genotypes (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from mixed BM chimeras shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Itpkb-/- thymocytes show a cell-intrinsically altered β-selection not rescued by a WT environment and the presence of WT thymocytes.
source: Thus, Itpkb-/- thymocytes show a cell-intrinsically altered β-selection not rescued by a WT environment and the presence of WT thymocytes.
evidence: This is inferred from the mixed BM chimera data showing that Itpkb-/- cells maintain their phenotype in a WT environment.

claim: Mathematical modeling suggests that a two fold or larger increase in the rate constants for DN3 to DN4 to ISP to DP transitions can cause reduced DN4 and ISP numbers but normal DN3 and DP cell numbers.
source: Indeed, mathematical modeling suggests that a two fold or larger increase in the rate constants for the successive transitions from DN3 to DN4 to ISP to DP cells with unaltered rates for progenitor development to DN3 cells, and for thymocyte turnover due to proliferation and death, can cause similarly reduced DN4 cell and ISP numbers but normal DN3 and DP cell numbers as seen in Itpkb-/- vs. WT mice (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by mathematical modeling results shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: Itpkb-/- fetal thymi had reduced overall DN and DN4 cell proportions on E16.5.
source: Consistent with faster thymocyte development, Itpkb-/- fetal thymi had reduced overall DN and DN4 cell proportions but higher DP cell proportions and total numbers than WT controls on embryonic day 16.5 (E16.5) where DP cells are first detectable in WT mice, and on E17.5 despite 'catching up' WT DP cells (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from fetal thymi shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Itpkb-/- fetal thymi had higher DP cell proportions and total numbers than WT controls on E16.5.
source: Consistent with faster thymocyte development, Itpkb-/- fetal thymi had reduced overall DN and DN4 cell proportions but higher DP cell proportions and total numbers than WT controls on embryonic day 16.5 (E16.5) where DP cells are first detectable in WT mice, and on E17.5 despite 'catching up' WT DP cells (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from fetal thymi shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Itpkb-/- fetal thymi had higher DP cell proportions and total numbers than WT controls on E17.5.
source: Consistent with faster thymocyte development, Itpkb-/- fetal thymi had reduced overall DN and DN4 cell proportions but higher DP cell proportions and total numbers than WT controls on embryonic day 16.5 (E16.5) where DP cells are first detectable in WT mice, and on E17.5 despite 'catching up' WT DP cells (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from fetal thymi shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: α-CD3 injection triggered progressive accumulation of DN4, ISP and DP cells 2 and 3 days later in both Rag2-/- and Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- genotypes.
source: α-CD3 injection triggered progressive accumulation of DN4, ISP and DP cells 2 and 3 days later in both genotypes (Figure 6C–F).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from α-CD3 injected Rag2-/- mice shown in Figure 6C-F.

claim: Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- mice accumulated larger proportions of DN4, ISP and DP cells than Rag2-/- mice on day 2 post α-CD3 injection.
source: However, Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- mice accumulated larger proportions of DN4 (33% vs. 18%), ISP (3% vs. 1%) and DP cells (20% vs. 1%) than Rag2-/- mice on day 2 when Rag2-/- mice barely had any DP cells.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from α-CD3 injected Rag2-/- mice shown in Figure 6C-F.

claim: Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- mice continued to accumulate more DP cells towards an ~four fold excess over Rag2-/- controls on day 3 post α-CD3 injection.
source: Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- mice continued to accumulate more DP cells towards an ~four fold excess over Rag2-/- controls on day 3 (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Both Rag2-/- and Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- genotypes showed similar thymocyte subset viability post α-CD3 injection.
source: This resulted mostly from faster development, as both genotypes showed similar thymocyte subset viability and proliferation post α-CD3 injection (Figure 6G,H).
evidence: This is supported by Annexin V staining data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Both Rag2-/- and Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- genotypes showed similar thymocyte subset proliferation post α-CD3 injection.
source: This resulted mostly from faster development, as both genotypes showed similar thymocyte subset viability and proliferation post α-CD3 injection (Figure 6G,H).
evidence: This is supported by Ki67 staining data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: α-CD3 injection upregulated surface CD2, CD5, CD71 and CXCR4 on DN3 and DN4 cells in Rag2-/- and Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- mice 2 days later.
source: Compared to uninjected Rag2-/- controls, α-CD3 injection upregulated surface CD2, CD5, CD71 and CXCR4 on DN3 and, more pronounced, on DN4 cells in Rag2-/- and Itpkb-/- Rag2-/- mice 2 days later (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: All activation markers reached higher surface-levels on Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- than Rag2-/- DN3 and DN4 cells after α-CD3 injection.
source: All markers reached higher surface-levels on Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- than Rag2-/- DN3 and DN4 cells.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: Higher Nr4a1/Nur77-GFP induction in Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- than Rag2-/- mice confirmed increased CD3 signaling.
source: Higher Nr4a1/Nur77-GFP induction in Itpkb-/- Rag2-/- than Rag2-/- mice confirmed increased CD3 signaling (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: WT and Itpkb-/- TCRβ- pre-selection DN3 cells had similar basal amounts of phosphorylated active Akt, mTOR and S6 protein.
source: Compared to negative controls and positive controls treated with the phosphatase-inhibitor Calyculin A (Pozuelo-Rubio et al., 2010), WT and Itpkb-/- TCRβ- pre-selection DN3 cells had significant but similar basal amounts of phosphorylated active Akt, mTOR and downstream S6 protein (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: TCRβ+ DN3 cells undergoing β-selection upregulated phospho-Akt, -mTOR, -S6 and control -Erk.
source: TCRβ+ DN3 cells undergoing β-selection upregulated phospho-Akt, -mTOR, -S6 and control -Erk, indicating pre-TCR mediated activation.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Phospho-Akt, -mTOR and -S6 but not -Erk levels were higher in Itpkb-/- than WT TCRβ+ DN3 and DN3-4 cells.
source: Importantly, and contrasting with a WT-like total Akt protein content in Itpkb-/- cells, phospho-Akt, -mTOR and -S6 but not -Erk levels were higher in Itpkb-/- than WT TCRβ+ DN3 and DN3-4 cells (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Itpkb-/- cells had WT-like total Akt protein content.
source: Importantly, and contrasting with a WT-like total Akt protein content in Itpkb-/- cells, phospho-Akt, -mTOR and -S6 but not -Erk levels were higher in Itpkb-/- than WT TCRβ+ DN3 and DN3-4 cells (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Itpkb-/- TCRβ+ DN3 and DN3-4 cells showed Glut-1 hyperinduction compared to WT controls.
source: Metabolic activation appeared increased in Itpkb-/- TCRβ+ DN3 and DN3-4 cells, because they showed Glut-1 hyperinduction and increased large cell proportions over WT controls (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Itpkb-/- TCRβ+ DN3 and DN3-4 cells showed increased large cell proportions compared to WT controls.
source: Metabolic activation appeared increased in Itpkb-/- TCRβ+ DN3 and DN3-4 cells, because they showed Glut-1 hyperinduction and increased large cell proportions over WT controls (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: α-CD3 injection hyperinduced surface CD71 on DN3 and DN4 cells in Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- versus Rag2-/- mice.
source: Moreover, α-CD3 injection hyperinduced surface CD71 on DN3 and DN4 cells in Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- versus Rag2-/- mice (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: Akt-inhibitor VIII treatment yielded Itpkb-/- DP cell proportions similar to those of untreated or carrier-treated WT controls after 4-day co-culture on OP9DL1 stroma.
source: Strikingly, all three treatments yielded Itpkb-/- DP cell proportions similar to those of untreated or carrier-treated WT controls after 4-day co-culture (Figure 9A, Figure 9—figure supplement 1A,C,E).
evidence: This is supported by data from OP9DL1 co-culture experiments shown in Figure 9A and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: Rapamycin treatment yielded Itpkb-/- DP cell proportions similar to those of untreated or carrier-treated WT controls after 4-day co-culture on OP9DL1 stroma.
source: Strikingly, all three treatments yielded Itpkb-/- DP cell proportions similar to those of untreated or carrier-treated WT controls after 4-day co-culture (Figure 9A, Figure 9—figure supplement 1A,C,E).
evidence: This is supported by data from OP9DL1 co-culture experiments shown in Figure 9A and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: 2-deoxy-D-glucose treatment yielded Itpkb-/- DP cell proportions similar to those of untreated or carrier-treated WT controls after 4-day co-culture on OP9DL1 stroma.
source: Strikingly, all three treatments yielded Itpkb-/- DP cell proportions similar to those of untreated or carrier-treated WT controls after 4-day co-culture (Figure 9A, Figure 9—figure supplement 1A,C,E).
evidence: This is supported by data from OP9DL1 co-culture experiments shown in Figure 9A and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: Rapamycin completely reversed the accelerated DN-to-DP development in Itpkb-/- versus Itpkb+/+ FTOC.
source: Similarly complete rapamycin reversal of the accelerated DN-to-DP development in Itpkb-/- versus Itpkb+/+ FTOC confirmed these important findings in a less reductionist system (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is supported by data from fetal thymic organ culture experiments shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: Itpkb-/- DN3 cells efficiently generated DP cells on OP9 stroma lacking Notch ligands.
source: In striking contrast, Itpkb-/- DN3 cells efficiently generated DP cells on OP9 stroma (Figures 7A,B, 9B, Figure 9—figure supplement 1B,D,F).
evidence: This is supported by data from OP9 co-culture experiments shown in Figures 7A,B, 9B and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: Inhibition of Akt, mTOR or glycolysis strongly reduced DP cell output from Itpkb-/- DN3 cells on OP9 stroma.
source: Inhibition of Akt, mTOR or glycolysis strongly reduced DP cell output.
evidence: This is supported by data from OP9 co-culture experiments with inhibitors shown in Figure 9B and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: LY-411,575 strongly impaired the α-CD3 induced DN cell development into ISP and DP cells in Rag2-/- but not Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- mice.
source: We found that LY-411,575 strongly impaired the α-CD3 induced DN cell development into ISP and DP cells in Rag2-/- but not Itpkb-/-Rag2-/- mice (Figure 10).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from γ-secretase inhibitor treated mice shown in Figure 10.

claim: Itpkb-loss reduces the Notch-dependence of DN thymocyte development to DP cells both in vitro and in vivo.
source: Hence, Itpkb-loss reduces the Notch-dependence of DN thymocyte development to DP cells both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the OP9 co-culture data and the γ-secretase inhibitor experiments.

claim: Itpkb is a novel pre-TCR effector which restricts the kinetics of β-selection.
source: Here, we identify Itpkb as a novel pre-TCR effector which restricts the kinetics of β-selection and establishes its Notch-dependence.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by all the experimental data.

claim: Itpkb establishes the Notch-dependence of β-selection.
source: Here, we identify Itpkb as a novel pre-TCR effector which restricts the kinetics of β-selection and establishes its Notch-dependence.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by all the experimental data.

claim: Itpkb-/- mice show a cell-autonomously accelerated and Notch independent, but pre-TCR dependent DN3-to-DP cell differentiation.
source: Itpkb-/- mice show a cell-autonomously accelerated and Notch independent, but pre-TCR dependent DN3-to-DP cell differentiation associated with DN3 cell pre-TCR hyperresponsiveness, Akt/mTOR hyperactivation and evidence for metabolic hyperactivity.
evidence: This is supported by data from multiple experimental systems including mixed BM chimeras, OP9 co-cultures, and γ-secretase inhibitor experiments.

claim: Pharmacologic inhibition of Akt, mTOR or glucose metabolism restored WT kinetics and Notch-dependence of Itpkb-/- DN3-to-DP cell development.
source: Pharmacologic inhibition of Akt, mTOR or glucose metabolism restored WT kinetics and Notch-dependence of Itpkb-/- DN3-to-DP cell development.
evidence: This is supported by data from OP9 co-culture experiments with inhibitors shown in Figures 7C,D and 9.

claim: Pre-TCR induced IP4/PIP3 antagonism governs β-selection by restricting PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling and metabolic activation.
source: Thus, we propose that pre-TCR induced IP4/PIP3 antagonism governs β-selection by restricting PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling and metabolic activation.
evidence: This is the proposed mechanism based on the experimental data and prior knowledge about IP4/PIP3 antagonism.

claim: Itpkb controls pre-TCR/Notch crosstalk through combined restriction of pre-TCR induced and Notch induced PI3K signaling via Akt.
source: We derive a model where Itpkb controls pre-TCR/Notch crosstalk through combined restriction of pre-TCR induced and Notch induced PI3K signaling via Akt (Figure 11).
evidence: This is the proposed model based on the experimental data, illustrated in Figure 11.

claim: Itpkb enforced coincidence detection of pre-TCR expression and Notch-engagement ensures that Akt is only activated to the degree needed for β-selection and only in an appropriate context.
source: Itpkb enforced coincidence detection of pre-TCR surface expression and Notch-engagement ensures that Akt is only activated to the degree needed for β-selection and only in an appropriate context, pre-TCR+ DN3 cells interacting with Notch-ligand expressing subcapsular stromal cells (Petrie and Zuniga-Pflucker, 2007).
evidence: This is the proposed mechanism based on the experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: Itpkb enforced coincidence detection prevents premature differentiation.
source: This prevents premature differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the accelerated differentiation phenotype of Itpkb-/- cells.

claim: Itpkb-/- E15.5 fetal thymic organ cultures produced more DP cells than WT controls.
source: Finally, Itpkb-/- E15.5 fetal thymic organ cultures (FTOC) produced more DP cells than WT controls (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is supported by data from fetal thymic organ culture experiments shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: WT DN3 cells much less efficiently generated DP cells without than with Notch.
source: As previously described (Ciofani and Zuniga-Pflucker, 2005; Xiong et al., 2011), WT DN3 cells much less efficiently generated DP cells without than with Notch (Figures 7A,B, 9A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data from OP9 vs OP9DL1 co-culture experiments shown in Figures 7A,B and 9A,B, and is consistent with prior publications.

claim: Inhibition of Akt, mTOR or glucose-metabolism further reduced WT DP cell production on OP9 stroma.
source: Inhibition of Akt, mTOR or Glucose-metabolism further reduced WT DP cell production consistent with known Akt, mTOR and glycolysis requirements for DN thymocyte survival and differentiation (Lee et al., 2012; Fayard et al., 2010; Juntilla and Koretzky, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by data from OP9 co-culture experiments with inhibitors shown in Figure 9B and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.
